answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. When linked accounts behave like one operator—reusing payment paths or coordinating claims—the protocol can slash their deposits and cap the shared reputation gain. This makes a sybil farm costly: the attacker must tie up real capital across accounts and risks losing it, while a meadow of honest agents can build trust gradually rather than accept a fable of instant credibility. The penalty also sends a ripple through the attacker’s remaining stake.
